sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: The Brazil-nut tree is a very large Amazonian canopy tree of non-flooded forest, commonly reported at about 25–56 m tall, with a massive trunk. Its hard woody capsule is roughly 11–16 cm across and contains about 10–25 large seeds, the Brazil nuts.

sections.title: Seeds and nutrition
sections.text: The seeds are eaten raw or processed. Their selenium content varies substantially by origin; a few nuts can provide a high amount, and excessive selenium intake is harmful. The plate's tall tree, hard capsule and large seeds match the species.
